headline: Dominated the ball.
Lost 0–2.
story.lead: United controlled it and did not convert it. 84% of the final-third possession, 21 shots to 8, 41 touches in their box against 11 in ours — and expected goals of 1.81 to 1.59, because the chances were not the same kind.
story.sub: This is the shape of last season repeated. Across 25/26 United won all 10 matches in which they held under 45% of the ball, and took 1.40 points per game in the 15 where they held over 55%. One match cannot confirm a trend — every 26/27 figure on this page carries its sample count.

hero.note: Season average 51 · highest of either season

story.shots_intro: Each circle is a shot, sized by expected goals. United’s 21 mapped shots came to 1.81 xG — 0.086 a shot. Twelve’s headline chance-quality figure of 0.10 divides the same 1.81 by 19 open-play shots, so the two are not interchangeable. Hull took 8 for 1.59, at 0.20 a shot, and scored both of their set-piece chances.
story.sits_note: Four of Hull’s eight shots were set pieces, worth 1.17 xG between them. Both goals came from that column.

kpis.note: Season average 51 · highest of either season

quadrant.note: Top right is doing both. Hull sat deep, so box presence was the scarce resource.
